note.title: The Journey Begins
note.overview: Aeneas gathers the surviving Trojans. The Greeks hold Troy, so the Trojans must leave and find a new homeland.
learningGoals: Recall the taught forms and facts independently.
Apply them to translation and GCSE-style questions.
Use the answer and individual mark points to improve precision.
summary: Aeneas gathers the surviving Trojans. The Greeks hold Troy, so the Trojans must leave and find a new homeland.
The men and women shout; the boys and girls cry. Preserve all four groups and assign each the correct reaction.
Aeneas leads them away. They quickly build ships and sail to Thrace. A supported interpretation is that they accept his leadership because they follow him and act on the plan.

quickCheck.question: Line 1: Whom did Aeneas gather?
quickCheck.stimulus:
The Journey Begins · classroom extract

1. Aeneas Troianos reliquos collexit.
2. “Graeci” inquit “Troiam nunc habent. discedere debemus. dei Troianos iubent novam patriam invenire.”
3. Troiani verba Aeneae audiverunt. viri feminaeque clamabant; pueri puellaeque lacrimabant.
4. Aeneas Troianos Troia duxit.
5. Troiani naves celeriter aedificaverunt et ad Thraciam navigaverunt.

Vocabulary: reliquos = remaining / surviving; collexit = gathered; inquit = said; iubent = order; verba = words; Aeneae = of Aeneas; audiverunt = heard; duxit = led; Troia = from Troy; celeriter = quickly; Thraciam = Thrace
